preamble: An isolated replacement of intervocalic [h] by [n] is reported for the Naskapi-Montagnais (Mushuau Innu) speech of Davis Inlet, Labrador, in the sequence -ahi-: words such as masinahikan 'book' and mahikan 'wolf' are pronounced with n instead of h. MacKenzie suggests an indirect path, -ahi- > -ayi- (intervocalic h becomes y in other dialects) followed by the local change y > [n], so the change is a single-dialect development rather than a direct glottal-to-nasal shift.

examples.note: Before a high front vowel; dialects retaining intervocalic h keep -ahi-.
MacKenzie proposes -ahi- > -ayi- > [ani], via the general Davis Inlet change y > [n].

sources: MacKenzie, M. E. (1980). Towards a Dialectology of Cree-Montagnais-Naskapi (Doctoral dissertation, University of Toronto), Chapter 2, p. 85. https://www.innu-aimun.ca/Docs/Other%20Resources/Academic%20Papers/MM/4_Chapter_2.pdf
